messages.subject: setting some thresholds equal
parts:
Dear Lavaan users,

 

I know what to do, if I want to set two intercepts to be equal:

var1 ~ a*1   

 var2 ~ a*1

 

Now I want to do the same with two thresholds, but I can’t treat them as intercepts. I tried to call them like they are shown in the output (“var1|t1”), but it didn’t function.

Does anybody know how to do it?

 

Thanks!

 Edgar Schoreit

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: setting some thresholds equal
parts:
On 07/09/2013 01:22 PM, Edgar Schoreit wrote:
> Dear Lavaan users,
>
> I know what to do, if I want to set two intercepts to be equal:
>
> var1 ~ a*1
>
> var2 ~ a*1
>
> Now I want to do the same with two thresholds, but I canï¿½t treat them as
> intercepts. I tried to call them like they are shown in the output

> (ï¿½var1|t1ï¿½), but it didnï¿½t function.

something like:

var1 | a*t1
var2 | a*t1
var3 | a*t1
var4 | a*t1

where var1-var4 are the variable names, and 't1' is used to denote the
'first threshold'

Yves.
